quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Electric results briefing Q&A: FY2025 year-end results briefing Q&A summary (05-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (year-end results briefing Q&A summary, May 22, 2026) on Infocommunications capacity: the new mid-term sales target for the segment reflects a considerable increase in customer demand and secured visibility on the production capacity to meet it; the main driver of the planned sales growth is volume. The data-center product capacity plan presented in November has been revised upward through additional capex and productivity gains; as demand keeps rising the company will add more through productivity and is considering further investment. Management sees high investment appetite continuing at all hyperscalers. Some optical wiring processes will use outsourcing, which costs more than in-house production, and the company will work to raise its in-house ratio. Optical connector capacity can be raised further with a relatively short lead time if demand exceeds plan. For optical devices and compound semiconductor substrates, customers' outlooks to 2030 mean capacity must double again from fiscal 2028 (company numbering), and the company is considering measures.
quarterly_data.figure: Optical device / substrate capacity to double again from fiscal 2028 (company numbering)

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Electric results briefing Q&A: FY2025 year-end results briefing Q&A summary (05-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (year-end results briefing Q&A summary) on CPO: the high-power CW-LD (continuous-wave laser diode) for co-packaged optics is now at the stage of final sample shipments and qualification and is under discussion with multiple customers; pilot shipments are expected to start at the end of fiscal 2026 (company numbering) with a ramp from fiscal 2027. From the device side, customers are evaluating CPO and conventional pluggables in parallel, so management takes a cautious view on whether CPO will ramp sharply right away. For CPO-related optical wiring products, the company has been selected as an NVIDIA development partner and continues development, with some sales expected from 2027 to 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: CW-LD for CPO pilot shipments from end of fiscal 2026 (company numbering), ramp from fiscal 2027; CPO wiring product sales from 2027 to 2028

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Electric results briefing Q&A: FY2025 year-end results briefing Q&A summary (05-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (year-end results briefing Q&A summary) on optical fiber and wiring: its MMC connector achieves high low-loss performance by combining ferrule precision with fiber outer-diameter precision, which management sees as a technical advantage, and MMC capacity has been expanded to meet customer demand; customers also value its rack-wiring design and efficient installation solutions for data centers. The company has preform capacity because it has long sold preforms to overseas fiber-drawing makers; it will raise fiber supply by buying fiber back from those drawing makers and expanding in-house drawing capacity. Any decision to expand preform capacity would come within the current mid-term plan; study has started and a decision will follow an assessment of demand from fiscal 2029, and the plan's capex does not include preform investment. Multi-core fiber development is progressing, but adoption is later than assumed because customers want to bring data centers up as fast as possible.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sumitomo Electric results briefing Q&A: FY2025 year-end results briefing Q&A summary (05-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (year-end results briefing Q&A summary) on the mid-term plan to fiscal 2028 (company numbering): the cumulative JPY 1 trillion capex breaks down roughly as Environment and Energy just under 20%, Infocommunications about 25%, Automotive about 40%, and Electronics and Industrial Materials just under 10% each. Infocommunications is planned to become the largest profit contributor at a 40% share, above Automotive, in line with the president's aim of cutting Automotive to below 50%; Infocommunications ROIC is expected to approach 40%, giving the company-wide 15% target. Automotive: orders are expected to rise gradually from 2026 to 2028, the vehicle models through fiscal 2028 are already decided so the sales target is seen as achievable, and the operating margin of about 6% today is targeted at 6.8% in fiscal 2028, aiming near 7%, through DX- and AI-based cost reduction. In fiscal 2026 higher labour costs are planned to be offset by price pass-through and cost reduction. Environment and Energy: power-cable sales rise year by year; the new European base starts mass production in fiscal 2027, manufacturing for the recently announced German DC35 project starts in fiscal 2028, and the European business ramps fully from fiscal 2027 and expands further from fiscal 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 1 trillion: Infocommunications about 25%, Automotive about 40%; Infocommunications 40% of profit; ROIC target 15%; Automotive margin target 6.8%
